terms.definition: A collection method that gives you each item together with its position number.

terms.definition: A function that walks through two sequences at the same time and pairs their items.
terms.example: Use zip to match each name with its score.

let names = ["Mina", "Jake"]
let ids = [1, 2]
print(Array(zip(names, ids)))

dialogue.title: Numbers, pairs and functions

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, I need the number of each name in my `names` list.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use Enumerated. It gives you each item with its position.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I wrote a counter by hand. Is Enumerated better?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, no manual counter. You get `i` and `n` in the loop.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. But I also have `ids`. How do I match them with `names`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use Zip. It walks through both arrays and pairs the items.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So Zip also gives me the positions?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, Enumerated gives positions. Zip only pairs two lists.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. And `map` takes a closure, so is it a Higher-Order Function?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. A Higher-Order Function takes or returns another function.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So `ids.map` is a Higher-Order Function that makes `doubled`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Enumerated for positions, Zip for pairs.
Use enumerated to show the step number next to each task.
